value.deck: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now offers Copilot Memory for persistent context and Ollama integration, boosting productivity and privacy for developers using open-source models.
shortVersion: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains IDEs has received a significant update, bringing two powerful new features: Copilot Memory and Ollama integration. These additions aim to enhance the developer experience, offering more intelligent and flexible AI assistance directly within the JetBrains environment.

Copilot Memory is a feature that allows Copilot to retain context about your project and preferences across different coding sessions. This means the AI can remember past interactions and project specifics, leading to more relevant and personalized code suggestions over time.

The new Ollama integration enables developers to run local open-source models as backends for code completions. This is particularly beneficial for environments requiring air-gapped security or strict data privacy, aligning with the growing trend of leveraging local AI for sensitive work.
value.plainLanguage: GitHub Copilot in JetBrains IDEs now remembers your project context and can use local AI models, making coding assistance smarter and more private.

keyTerms.meaning: An AI feature that stores information about your coding projects and personal preferences, allowing the AI to provide more consistent and relevant suggestions across different work sessions.

A platform that lets you run large language models (LLMs) on your local machine, enabling developers to use open-source AI models for tasks like code completion without sending data to external servers.
A suite of popular integrated development environments (IDEs) like IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm, widely used by professional developers for various programming languages.

Computer systems or networks that are physically isolated from unsecured networks, like the internet, to prevent data breaches and ensure maximum security, often requiring local-only software solutions.

value.whyItMatters: This update is crucial for JetBrains developers as it brings their GitHub Copilot experience to parity with VS Code, offering advanced productivity features like persistent context and enabling the use of local, privacy-focused AI models for sensitive projects, a significant step in the broader trend of localized AI development.
